Elamon has two parts: this app, and elamond, a small service on the computer you want to watch. It reads the computer\'s own counters and sends them only to phones you paired with it; if you allow it, it also lets them control the computer. It needs no root and runs as your user. Everything is set on the computer, in elamond.toml: the dashboards, what a phone may run, and how the app looks and behaves on each phone. The app only draws what the service describes.

Without a firewall nothing needs opening. If ufw is on:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. Otherwise open TCP %1$s and UDP %2$s in the one you use.

TCP %1$s is the Elamon service itself. UDP %2$s is mDNS, which lets the app find the computer by itself; without it, add the computer by its address. Over a VPN such as Tailscale or WireGuard only %1$s matters, and a trusted VPN interface needs nothing.

It shows a QR code and a six-digit code, good for five minutes. Point the phone\'s camera at the QR code and open the link: that pairs in one tap. The link carries the computer\'s addresses and, after them, names that stay when addresses change: its Tailscale name, and any set as names in elamond.toml.

Or in this app tap the computer under Found on this network, or Add computer and its address or host name, and enter the code. The app first shows the computer\'s certificate digits: they must match the Certificate line on the computer.
The computer isn\'t under Found on this network

The phone and the computer have to be on the same network, with UDP %1$s open on the computer. VPNs and many guest Wi-Fi networks block this kind of discovery. Add the computer by address or name instead: elamond pair shows them.
Check that the service runs, and read its log:
Then check that TCP %1$s is open in the firewall and that the phone can reach the computer\'s address.

The app says the certificate changed

The service made a new certificate it can\'t vouch for: its folder ~/.local/share/elamon was deleted, or the system was reinstalled. If so, restore a backup made with elamond backup, or forget the computer in the app and pair again. If not, something else may be answering at that address; check the network first. A certificate renewed with elamond rotate-cert is different: the app checks that the old one signed it and follows by itself.
Some sensors need kernel modules. lm-sensors finds and loads them; then restart the service:
The graphics card shows no load

NVIDIA cards need NVIDIA\'s driver, whose management library the service reads. A card marked Sleeping is powered down and is left that way until a program uses it. Intel graphics don\'t report their load without extra privileges, so the app shows the clock instead.
A monitor that is switched off or blanked has no mode. If no monitor shows one, the service can\'t open the graphics device: your user has to be logged in at the computer or be in the video group.
How do I unpair a phone?
In the app: the computer\'s menu, Forget computer. To also drop the phone\'s access on the computer, list the paired phones and revoke one by its ID:
How do I move to a new phone?

On the old phone: Settings → Export pairings, a passphrase, and where to save the file. Copy the file to the new phone, install Elamon there and choose Settings → Import pairings. The file is encrypted with the passphrase and can\'t be opened without it.

Each computer gives the new phone a key of its own, with the same role, the next time the app reaches it: elamond clients then lists it beside the old phone, as added with the key of the old phone\'s ID. Moving for good, forget the computers on the old phone or reset it, and revoke that ID; the new phone keeps working:

A computer that takes no more phones, or whose old phone\'s key gave its one key of its own to another phone already, can\'t give it one: there both phones stay one entry, and revoking it cuts off both. Then pair the new phone again with elamond pair (the app replaces the computer), and revoke the old entry.
How do I move to a new computer, or reinstall this one?
Back up the service before; it asks for a passphrase:
On the new or reinstalled system, install the service, then stop it, restore the backup and start it again. The phones connect as before, without pairing again:
To bring back elamond.toml and the files in elamond.d too, restore with:

The Control tab opens links and starts what\'s behind them, plays music, switches the power profile, runs commands and powers the computer off. It\'s off until you allow it on the computer; then each phone may do what its role allows (elamond clients role):
On NixOS, in the service\'s settings. control.users also lets power actions and the power profile through without a password:

Links to the web pages the computer hosts show up in the Control tab with their state: tap one to open it, hold it for its details and to start, stop or restart its unit. They are set on the computer only:
Commands are defined only on the computer, so a phone can\'t run anything else; a phone chooses only among the values a parameter allows. Each becomes a button in the app, and its output comes back:

Elsewhere, power actions and system units need a polkit rule, because the service runs outside a login session. Without it the app marks them \"needs permission\". Save this as /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/50-elamon.rules, with your user name:

Before power, ending processes, units and the computer\'s actions, the app asks to unlock the phone with a fingerprint, the face or the screen lock. The phone\'s profile on the computer chooses which actions ask (unlock.for) and how long an unlock lasts (unlock.grace); an action\'s own unlock = true always asks.

Optional, at the top of ~/.config/elamon/elamond.toml; elamond check says what is wrong in it. Where the service listens and how often it reads, with their defaults:
the TCP port the app connects to
the addresses or interfaces to listen on, one or a list such as [\"tailscale0\", \"192.168.200.10\"]; \"::\" covers every address, IPv4 and IPv6
the name shown in the app; the host name when empty
announce the service on the local network, so the app finds it
minutes of history a phone gets when it connects
The service keeps its certificate and the paired phones in ~/.local/share/elamon. Deleting that folder unpairs every phone; elamond backup keeps a copy that elamond restore puts back.

The phone talks to your computer directly, encrypted, and trusts only the certificate it saw when pairing. Nothing passes through any server, and the app has no trackers, ads or analytics. Each phone has its own key, which the computer can revoke; on the phone it is sealed with a key that never leaves Android\'s key store, and kept out of backups; Export pairings writes it only into a file encrypted with your passphrase. Unless control is turned on, the service only reads; with it on, it acts as your user, and every action is logged with the name of the phone that asked.

What the app shows is set on the computer. The service has standard dashboards built in (the overview, processes, sensors, control, and the pages their tiles open) and a default profile. To see them, as a starting point for your own:

Settings go in ~/.config/elamon/elamond.toml, or in files of their own in ~/.config/elamon/elamond.d. A dashboard, an action or a profile with the id of a built-in one changes only the keys it gives. A dashboard of your own, and a profile that makes it a tab:
Check the settings before the service reads them; elamond edit opens the file in your editor and keeps it only once it reads. elamond values lists what this computer can show:

A profile says how the app looks and behaves on a phone: theme, colours, animations, how often it asks, what it confirms and unlocks for, and which dashboards are its tabs. Give a phone its profile by the phone\'s ID from elamond clients; it applies at once:
The app\'s Settings show what applies on each computer, and the key each line comes from.
